headline: Akbar Ali's unexplained absence from 63 touring squads raises questions of dissent
summary: Despite leading Bangladesh to an U-19 World Cup title and having significant domestic experience, the wicketkeeper-batter was overlooked for all recent tours, fueling speculation about non-cricketing factors.
details: Cricket selection typically follows clear logic like form and fitness. However, the conspicuous absence of domestic cricket leader Akbar Ali from Bangladesh's recent touring squads has raised questions. Between July and September, 63 players were sent abroad for various tours, with selectors extensively drawing from the domestic pool.

Akbar, a 24-year-old wicketkeeper-batter with considerable domestic experience, was not included in any of these squads, instead playing club cricket in England. While his recent numbers aren't overwhelming, his complete exclusion from such a large touring program is notable. He scored 217 runs in nine innings at an average of 24.11 in the 2025-26 Dhaka Premier Division Cricket League.

Earlier, he captained Rangpur Division to a domestic double and scored 121 for North Zone in the Bangladesh Cricket League. These performances, while not guaranteeing selection, make his complete absence from multiple squads, especially when other wicketkeeper-batters were given opportunities, a legitimate concern.

Akbar famously led Bangladesh to their first men's Under-19 World Cup title in 2020 and also captained Bangladesh at the Asia Cup Rising Stars last year. Beyond his current batting statistics, his proven leadership and experience are significant assets as a cricketer.

Chief selector Habibul Bashar previously stated that Akbar remains in Bangladesh's plans, assuring that selectors know "what he is capable of." This assurance, however, contradicts his complete oversight during a period of extensive international touring.

This unanswered question has fueled speculation that factors beyond cricket may be at play. Sources suggest Akbar was involved in disagreements within the Cricketers Welfare Association of Bangladesh (CWAB) as an executive committee member. He allegedly expressed dissenting positions on certain player issues, which reportedly did not sit well with association leaders.

There are also claims that Akbar’s name was initially considered for some overseas assignments but was later removed for reasons not purely cricketing. When recently questioned by reporters, Akbar remained diplomatic, rejecting any "conspiracy" narrative.

However, he admitted that being left out of every touring squad had caused him hurt. If concerns from players about career repercussions for dissenting opinions are accurate, this issue extends beyond Akbar Ali to the broader culture of Bangladesh cricket.

headline_marked: [[11-party alliance begins long march]] to Rangpur today with 8 demands including Teesta Master Plan
headline: 11-party alliance begins long march to Rangpur today with 8 demands including Teesta Master Plan
summary: The alliance expects 3-5 lakh people at the concluding rally in Rangpur, making it their second major program after a similar march to Chattogram. They urge the government not to obstruct the peaceful demonstration.
details: The 11-party alliance, led by Jamaat-e-Islami, commenced its long march towards Rangpur today, Saturday, with an eight-point demand. This marks their second major program after a similar long march to Chattogram on September 5.

A key regional demand for the northern region, the implementation of the Teesta Master Plan, has been added to their agenda for this march. Other demands include ending corruption, land grabbing, extortion, and addressing national issues like price hikes and energy crises.

Alliance leaders anticipate a larger turnout for the Rangpur march compared to the Chattogram one, expecting 3 to 5 lakh people at the concluding rally in Rangpur Zila School ground. They also project thousands of vehicles will join the convoy from various districts along the route.

The long march began with an inaugural rally at Manik Mia Avenue in Dhaka at 7 AM, with the convoy departing for Rangpur at 8 AM. Path meetings are scheduled at multiple locations including Gazipur, Tangail, Sirajganj, Bogura, and Gaibandha, culminating in the Rangpur rally at 7 PM.

Leaders of the 11-party alliance have urged the government not to obstruct the long march and instructed their activists to maintain patience and restraint in the face of any provocation. They also expressed regret for any potential public inconvenience caused by the program.

The alliance's focus on Rangpur is strategic, given their strong electoral performance in the region during the 13th national parliamentary elections. Jamaat won 17 seats and the National Citizen's Party (NCP) won 2, totaling 19 seats for the alliance in the Rangpur division.

This series of long marches aims to bring national political demands to people across different regions of the country. Following Rangpur, the alliance has announced future long marches to Khulna on October 31 and Sylhet on November 21.
